cohort: Women (N = 150) who underwent elective cesarean delivery at Gynecological and Obstetrical University Hospital Sant'Anna, Turin, Italy, between March 2014 and July 2014
finding: The audit identified an excess in repeat cesarean sections, prompting the implementation of interventions that led to a significant reduction in the cesarean birth after cesarean (CBAC) rate.
